panels.title: Proxy
panels.description: Blackbox probe to the public proxy URL. The only check that reflects what a user experiences.

panels.title: Teleport targets responding
panels.description: Scrape targets answering, over the number that exist. Colour is percentage-based, so it stays correct as replicas change.

panels.title: Postgres
panels.description: postgres_exporter's own connection - independent of Teleport's view.

panels.title: Flux resources synced
panels.description: Flux resources matching Git. Below 100% means your changes are not landing.

panels.title: Login latency (p99)
panels.description: Time to issue a user certificate - what a person feels running tsh login. Rises under demand before anything else here.

panels.title: Backend write latency (p99)
panels.description: Cluster-state writes only. component=backend excludes the in-memory cache, which would hide real latency.

panels.title: Failed audit event writes (1h)
panels.description: Audit events Teleport could not write, counted over the preceding hour. Any non-zero value means records were lost.

panels.title: Pending session recording uploads
panels.description: Recordings whose upload has not completed. In-flight uploads count too, so brief non-zero is normal; sustained is not.

panels.title: Time to soonest cert expiry
panels.description: Soonest expiry across all cert-manager Certificates, including internal Postgres certs.

panels.title: Pods awaiting scheduling
panels.description: Anything unschedulable. Non-zero here preceded the Postgres outage during buildout.

panels.title: Largest CPU request that fits in every AZ
panels.description: Free cores on the roomiest node in the tightest AZ. EBS volumes are AZ-pinned, so cluster-wide headroom misleads. Thresholds assume 250m Teleport pods.

panels.title: Postgres connections in use
panels.description: Connections against max_connections, both read from Postgres. Pool exhaustion shows as Teleport write latency against an idle-looking database.

panels.title: CPU requested vs allocatable, by node
panels.description: Solid lines are requests, grey dashed are each node's ceiling. Requests drive scheduling - a node can be 90% requested and nearly idle.

panels.title: Schedulable CPU headroom, by zone
panels.description: Per-AZ free cores. A pod with an existing PV can only use headroom in its own zone.

targets.expr:
max by (label_topology_kubernetes_io_zone) (
  (
    sum by (node) (kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="cpu"})
    - sum by (node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu"})
  ) * on (node) group_left(label_topology_kubernetes_io_zone)
  max by (node, label_topology_kubernetes_io_zone) (kube_node_labels)
)

panels.title: Pending pods by namespace
panels.description: Total is a grey dashed reference line that is always present, so a flat zero means 'measured, nothing wrong'.

panels.title: Restarts and OOMKills (1h rolling)
panels.description: Crash loops versus memory pressure. The 1h window is fixed in the query, not the time picker.

panels.title: Arriving demand
panels.description: Work arriving per second. Certificate issuance counts logins; authenticated connections includes reconnects and non-login traffic.

panels.title: Concurrent sessions
panels.description: Sessions existing right now. Proxy count includes commands, scp and port-forwards; interactive counts only sessions with a shell attached.

panels.title: Login latency and failures
panels.description: p50 rising means everyone is slower; p99 alone means a suffering tail. Failures flat with latency climbing is capacity, not auth.

panels.title: Fleet and registered resources
panels.description: Adoption as estate rather than people. Missing tunnels are agents that should be connected and are not.

panels.title: Demand exceeding limits
panels.description: Demand that was refused rather than served. Any sustained value is users being turned away.

panels.title: Proxy throughput
panels.description: Volume through the proxy. Two users moving files and two hundred idle shells look identical by session count and nothing alike here.

panels.title: Demand vs backend work
panels.description: Backend work per unit of demand. Writes climbing faster than issuance means something other than logins drives the backend.

panels.title: CPU used vs demand
panels.description: Cores CONSUMED, against sessions. The Capacity row shows cores REQUESTED - the gap between them is where right-sizing lives.

panels.title: Memory used vs demand
panels.description: Expect memory NOT to track sessions: Teleport's footprint is dominated by its cache of cluster state, which scales with estate rather than traffic.

panels.title: Backend cost per session
panels.description: Flat under rising demand means linear scaling - buy capacity. Rising means each session costs more than it did, which capacity will not fix.

panels.title: Data transfer per session
panels.description: Rising here with flat session counts means sessions are getting heavier - file transfers rather than shells.

panels.title: Teleport: cluster-state backend
panels.description: Write conflicts are compare-and-swap retries when two writers hit the same key. Conflicts rising with flat latency is lock churn.

panels.title: Teleport: audit events to Postgres
panels.description: The audit path, separate from cluster state. Divergence from the panel beside it localises which half is struggling.

panels.title: Postgres server activity
panels.description: Server-side view. Teleport latency rising while this stays flat points at the pool or network, not the database.

panels.title: Uploads awaiting completion
panels.description: Counts, not rates. What matters is whether this returns to zero after sessions end.

panels.title: Audit event emission
panels.description: Failures here with S3 requests flat means Teleport never reached S3; failures alongside S3 errors means S3 rejected the write.

panels.title: S3 calls by operation
panels.description: Filtered to recording operations. Credential and health calls are excluded - widen the regex if you need them.

panels.title: S3 call latency
panels.description: Aggregated across operations. Add a label filter to isolate a slow one rather than drawing all of them.

panels.title: S3 requests (CloudWatch)
panels.description: S3's own view. Teleport-side errors with no S3 requests means the call was never made. Lags ~15 minutes.

panels.title: Reconcile failures and suspensions
panels.description: Named failures. A suspended resource is silent, intentional, and easy to forget mid-debug.

panels.title: Reconcile duration p99 by kind
panels.description: Rising duration precedes timeouts. A Kustomization with wait:true taking minutes is usually waiting on something that will never be ready.

panels.title: Public endpoint
panels.description: End-to-end to the public proxy URL. Healthy pods plus a failing probe points at the LB, DNS or security groups.

panels.title: Time to cert expiry
panels.description: 'Served by public endpoint' is the leaf cert the proxy actually presents. A gap from cert-manager means it renewed but was never reloaded.

panels.title: Distinct users
panels.description: Different people logging in, per bucket - active users, not users who have ever existed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  count(DISTINCT event_data->>'user') AS "distinct users"
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type = 'user.login'
  AND event_data->>'user' IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Logins by user
panels.description: Stacked per person: total height is volume, each band is one user. 6 of 102 login events carry no user and are excluded.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  event_data->>'user' AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type = 'user.login'
  AND event_data->>'user' IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Login outcome and method
panels.description: Successes by auth method, failures separate. 28 of 102 logins carry an error field.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  CASE WHEN event_data->>'success' = 'true'
       THEN coalesce(event_data->>'method', 'unknown')
       ELSE 'FAILED (' || coalesce(event_data->>'method', 'unknown') || ')'
  END AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type = 'user.login'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Instances joining, by role
panels.description: Agents registering, with failures called out. 42 of 220 join attempts carry an error - invisible elsewhere on this dashboard.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  CASE WHEN event_data->>'success' = 'true'
       THEN coalesce(event_data->>'role', 'unknown')
       ELSE 'FAILED (' || coalesce(event_data->>'role', 'unknown') || ')'
  END AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type = 'instance.join'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Session and app activity
panels.description: Logins far exceeding sessions means people authenticate without connecting to anything.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  event_type AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type IN ('session.start', 'app.session.start', 'user.login', 'session.upload')
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Access request workflow
panels.description: Expiries outnumbering reviews means requests go unanswered - an adoption blocker no infrastructure metric shows.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  event_type AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type LIKE 'access_request.%'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Security posture events
panels.description: MFA challenges issued versus validated. Challenges without validations means people are being prompted and abandoning.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  event_type AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type IN ('mfa_auth_challenge.create', 'mfa_auth_challenge.validate',
                     'device.authenticate', 'saml.created', 'role.deleted', 'role.updated')
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: SSH sessions by target host
panels.description: What people actually connect to, as opposed to what exists.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  coalesce(event_data->>'server_hostname', 'unknown') AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type = 'session.start'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: App sessions by application
panels.description: Almost entirely 'grafana' for now - every visit to this dashboard writes one of these events.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  coalesce(event_data->>'app_name', 'unknown') AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND event_type = 'app.session.start'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Access requests by role requested
panels.description: Roles unnested, so a two-role request counts against both. Shows where the RBAC model and actual need diverge.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(event_time, $__interval),
  r.role AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM events e
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements_text(e.event_data::jsonb -> 'roles') AS r(role)
WHERE $__timeFilter(e.event_time)
  AND e.event_type = 'access_request.create'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Users seen, cumulative
panels.description: Running count of distinct people who have ever logged in. Only ever rises - departures are not subtracted.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  first_seen AS time,
  count(*) OVER (ORDER BY first_seen) AS "users seen"
FROM (
  SELECT min(event_time) AS first_seen, event_data->>'user' AS u
  FROM events
  WHERE event_type = 'user.login' AND event_data->>'user' IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 2
) f
ORDER BY first_seen

panels.title: Roles defined, cumulative
panels.description: Distinct role names ever created. Deduplicated on name, so the operator's 1043 repeat role.created events count once each. VERIFY: assumes role.created carries a 'name' field.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  first_seen AS time,
  count(*) OVER (ORDER BY first_seen) AS "roles"
FROM (
  SELECT min(event_time) AS first_seen, event_data->>'name' AS r
  FROM events
  WHERE event_type = 'role.created' AND event_data->>'name' IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 2
) f
ORDER BY first_seen

panels.title: Joined instances by role, cumulative
panels.description: An 'instance' is a Teleport PROCESS joining - proxy, auth, agent or node - not a protected resource. Grouped on the singular 'role' field, present in all 220 events, rather than the 'roles' array which only 40 carry. Deduplicated on node_name because host_id is regenerated on every process start. Still approximate: agent pod names change on restart. For true inventory use the Teleport API, not the audit log.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  f.first_seen AS time,
  f.kind AS metric,
  count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY f.kind ORDER BY f.first_seen) AS value
FROM (
  SELECT min(event_time) AS first_seen,
         event_data->>'node_name' AS node_name,
         coalesce(event_data->>'role', 'unknown') AS kind
  FROM events
  WHERE event_type = 'instance.join'
    AND event_data->>'success' = 'true'
    AND event_data->>'node_name' IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 2, 3
) f
ORDER BY f.first_seen
